records.question: Can Expo Go prove a production-grade native application?
records.applicableRange: current Expo documentation as of 2026-07-22; recheck for the selected SDK
records.conclusion: No. Use development builds for production-grade development and internal/release builds for acceptance-sensitive native behavior.
records.contradiction: Course material occasionally treats a development/simulator visual pass as sufficient completion.

records.question: Where should an animated launch experience be verified?
records.applicableRange: Expo SDK 52 and newer behavior documented in current latest docs
records.conclusion: Verify the native splash on an internal or production build. Keep it visible only until content is ready; custom branding animation belongs in-app with reduced-motion handling.
records.contradiction: The course presents a fixed two-second generated video as the splash without separating native launch screen from in-app animation.

records.question: Which Supabase values may be bundled in an Expo mobile client?
records.applicableRange: current Supabase publishable/secret key model; legacy anon/service_role keys deprecated by end of 2026
records.conclusion: Bundle only project URL and publishable key. Secret/service-role keys and database passwords are backend-only and bypass RLS.
records.contradiction: The course puts service-role/DB credentials and a non-expiring management token in a project .env available to the agent.
records.enforcement: environment manifest secret boundary and audit

records.question: Is an Android keystore the application identifier?
records.applicableRange: Android app signing and OAuth identity model
records.conclusion: No. The application ID/package name identifies software; the keystore holds signing material; certificate fingerprints identify the signing certificate to OAuth and platform services.
records.contradiction: The course describes the keystore as the unique app identifier and SHA-1 as encryption.

records.question: How should EAS environment-variable visibility be selected?
records.applicableRange: current EAS environments and visibility model
records.conclusion: Classify each value as client-visible, sensitive build secret, server-only secret, or signing credential. Secret-visibility values are not available for client JS bundling; EXPO_PUBLIC values are public.
records.contradiction: The course treats one .env and interactive portal choices as a sufficient secret model.

records.question: What native verification contract does agent-device provide?
records.applicableRange: official site checked 2026-07-22; pin and re-read installed CLI help before use
records.conclusion: Use semantic snapshots, deterministic .ad replay, logs, recordings, screenshots, network evidence, and environment controls. The CLI is not currently installed in this workspace.
records.contradiction: The course defers or skips native E2E and uses manual taps as final evidence.
records.enforcement: pinned CLI preflight and agent-device-only E2E policy
